Workforce and rostering: the roster, the gap and the bank

Who is working, where the hole is, and what it cost to fill it, on one set of records — with the safe-staffing return rated exactly as the code holds it.

Live vs demonstrated: Live — real, API-backed platform logic (wired end-to-end today) Demonstrated — representative control surface with seeded data / illustrative UI mock-up
© 2026 Commvita Digital Health Solutions Ltd. All rights reserved.

1 The roster, the gap and the bank

Three questions run a service: who is working, where is the hole, and what did it cost to fill it. Most organisations answer them in three systems and reconcile in a spreadsheet. commvita answers them from one set of records, so the shift a manager filled on Tuesday is the row the pay bill counts and the row a safe-staffing return is built from.

First to market
Payroll runs against the contract register, with no separate HR system. A pay period reads the same contracts that hold the whole-time equivalent, the band and the pension scheme, so the run carries headcount and WTE with the gross, the employer national insurance and the pension. No system we assessed does payroll and the clinical operating record on one platform; the alternative is an HR system, an interface and a monthly reconciliation somebody owns.From commvita’s own competitive assessment of this module against the systems it competes with. Our assessment, not an independent one.

Build it

Week view · templates · rotations · self-rostering

Shifts by person and day, with the skill mix counted underneath. Patterns come from a template, doctors run on rotations, and staff put in preferences before sign-off.

Fill it

Bank pool · agency requests · tiers · rates

A bank of known people with their skills and hourly rate, then an agency request with a tier, a cost code and a rate if the bank cannot cover it. Filled or unfilled is a state on the record.

Answer for it

Working time · skill mix · CHPPD · pay

Working-time breaches and rest-period gaps come out of the same shifts, care hours per patient day are derived from them, and the pay bill sits next to both.

2 Building a roster

The week view is the roster as it stands: every person, every day, the shift code and its start time, with a qualified-staff count on the bottom row. It is written and read through the platform’s own rota records, so a change here is the change everything else sees.

1

Start from a pattern rather than a blank grid

A template holds a pattern and is applied to a chosen week. Doctors in training sit on rotations with a start and end date rather than being typed in each time. Neither is clever; both stop a week being rebuilt by hand.

/rostering/rota/templates/rota/rotations
2

Let staff say what they want before it is fixed

Self-rostering preferences go in against a week and come back accepted or not. Leave requests run against a live balance and the same week, so the two are never out of step.

/rota/self-roster-preferences/rota/leave-requests
3

Sign it off, and keep the provisional state visible

Until a roster is signed off it says so on the header. Sign-off is an action against the week, so “the roster was provisional when that shift ran” is a fact on the record.

/rota/sign-off

On-call and leave are the same records the member of staff sees in their own portal.

3 Filling a gap: bank first, then agency

A gap is only interesting once you know what it costs to close. commvita holds a bank pool of known people with skills and hourly rate, and an agency request register with a tier, a cost code, a rate and who filled it. The order is the point: bank before agency, and the cost of getting that order wrong is in the same table.

The two rates say more than a policy does. A bank clinician is on £22.50 an hour; the tier-one agency fill for the same role is £32. Both carry a cost code and both roll into the spend on the roster header. A separate cascade board at /bank-agency lays the escalation out with rate cards and working-time checks; it is a demonstrated surface with seeded content.

4 The rules the roster breaks

A roster that cannot tell you when it breaks the working-time rules is a diary. The compliance tab reads the same shifts over a seventeen-week reference period and marks breaches by name: contracted hours against hours this week, the seventeen-week average, the exception count, and a separate table of rest periods under eleven hours.

Skill mix is counted the same way: planned and actual whole-time equivalent, qualified against unqualified, and the bank and agency share of the week, all from the rostered shifts. Sickness is scored on the Bradford factor from the sick leave recorded.

Where the header is softer than the grid. On the strip of tiles above the roster, the fill, unfilled, bank and agency counts and the spend are counted from the records. Two of them, planned hours and roster compliance percentage, are fixed values returned by the platform rather than computed from the week in front of you. Better said here than quoted at a board meeting as something the roster produced.

5 CHPPD, and the honest state of the safe-staffing return

Care hours per patient day is the number a board reads and the one most often typed. In commvita it is derived and never stored: care hours come from shifts keyed to a ward, the denominator from occupied bed days, and the period is half open so the discharge day is not an occupied day.

Now the part this library has rated two different ways. That screen is a demonstrated surface: the ward rows, the RAG ratings and the escalations are seeded content held in the page, and the staffing board, the professional judgement log and the board return are the same. Rating them as live overstates what a buyer gets on day one, and this document settles it the other way.

1

The computation is real, and on this data it returns nothing

Ask for CHPPD over a week of the demonstration data and it returns an empty ward list, 840 care hours it will not attribute, and the reason: not one of the four hundred rostered shifts is keyed to a ward, because the seeded shifts sit at ambulance stations, clinics and community bases. A shift with no ward key contributes to nothing, and spreading it across wards would manufacture the number.

/safe-staffing/chppd/safe-staffing/occupancy
2

It tells you what is unkeyed and why

The reconciliation return names the staff it could not resolve and the shift locations that are not wards, so the gap is something an organisation can close rather than a percentage on a slide. A name held by two people resolves to nobody instead of to the first row.

/safe-staffing/phase0/reconciliation
3

What it refuses to report

There is no registered and support split, and it says so with its reason: the role on a shift is free text, and inferring a classification from a pay band would be a guess presented as a measurement. commvita ships none of the licensed acuity instruments either. It holds the judgement and the variance and never declares a shift safe.

NQB 2014NHS England 2019

6 Workforce intelligence, split down the middle

Vacancy, turnover, sickness and agency spend are the four numbers a workforce committee lives on. The page carries them twice: a live band computed from the record at the top, and an illustrative planning band underneath, labelled as seeded.

The live band reads contracted WTE from the contract register, the pay bill from payroll and sickness from recorded absence. Where nothing has been recorded it prints ND rather than nought, because a vacancy rate of nought per cent reads as a fully staffed organisation, and it names the fix: set a funded establishment for the period. It also refuses to estimate. Two filled agency requests carry a rate but no hours, so they are excluded from the cost rather than guessed at.

The seeded band is the planning view a buyer sees in a demonstration: turnover, time to hire, staff group against funded establishment, twelve months of headcount. It shows the shape of the reporting and it is not a read of the record. The page says so itself, in a banner at the top.

7 The visual boards

Ward by day is where a fill problem is visible. The heatmap puts roster fill for each ward against each day with a sickness marker on the shifts that carried one. Two more views sit behind it: a skill-mix treemap of substantive against bank and agency by staff group, and per-ward agency reliance against an eighty per cent substantive target.

Every figure there is illustrative and the page says so before you read a number. I keep it because the control surface is the thing being bought: the grouping, the thresholds, the accessible table behind the picture. The numbers follow once a deployment keys its shifts to wards.

8 What it costs, and who is trained to do it

Rostering that does not meet pay is half a system. commvita holds legal entities, cost centres with a budget and a named holder, contracts with band, WTE, hours and pension scheme, and payroll runs against those contracts.

These are records rather than a report. A contract can be added, a payroll run moved from draft to paid, and service line profit and loss reads the same cost centres. That is why the live band on the intelligence page can say there is no pay bill to express agency spend as a share of: it is reading this table and finding no row for the month.

First to market
Training compliance drawn on the organisation’s own care-group structure. Mandatory training is reported as a heatmap across the care groups the organisation built in its own hierarchy, so a director sees which part of the structure is behind rather than one trust-wide percentage. No other platform in this market ties the compliance view to the org structure that way. In this demonstration the figures behind the heatmap are seeded.From commvita’s own competitive assessment of this module against the systems it competes with. Our assessment, not an independent one.

The staff member’s side of this, their leave balance, their mandatory training and registration expiry, their CPD log, is one identity away in the Staff Portal. The rota a manager builds here is the rota that person sees there.

One more ceiling, plainly: the staff record integration at /esr-integration is a demonstrated surface. Snapshot, vacancy tracker, training sync and benchmarking run on seeded content and the page says so. No staff record feed is wired in this build.

What it is not. It is not an acuity instrument and it does not declare a shift safe. commvita reports the establishment, the roster, the variance and the judgement recorded against them; whether a shift can run is decided by the named nurse or manager running it. It is not a demand model either: the seven-day gap forecast is operational planning guidance built from unfilled shifts and recent absence. It carries no medical-device claim. Non-SaMD.
